Upload this file plus `docs/PRD.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/TASKS.md`. Say:
*"Continuing the English bot build. Read BUILD_PROGRESS.md. Give me the Cursor prompt for the next slice."*

Excluding A2 because "the learners are B1 heading for B2" **conflates *this word is rated easy* with *this learner already knows it***, which is precisely the conflation PRD §2.1 built the known-word ledger to prevent: an A2-tagged lemma at rank 3,500 is an uncommon word that happens to be simple in form, and whether either learner has met it is a question the **ledger** answers per learner, not one the tag answers for both. A1 stays out — a learner at B1 has A1 coverage by definition of being at B1, so there the tag really does predict the ledger. The two filters now do two separable jobs: `freq_rank > 2000` excludes what is assumed known, and the CEFR tag excludes proper nouns (`john` sits at rank 548 in a lowercased frequency list; only the tag tells it from a word). |

PRD §2.1's own vocabulary budget — 1,500–2,000 new known words over the 24 weeks against a 3,759-lemma pool — projects **40% to 53%** erosion by the end of the programme, so 60 held across most of the PRD's range and **failed at the top of it: 2,000 new words leaves 28**. And the units a learner reaches last are the ones that have eroded longest, so the failure would land on the learner who used the app most — #91's shape again. 65 raises the tolerance to 53.8% and covers the whole projected range. **It is also the ceiling the content supports**: stage 3 yields 263 lemmas and four units at 65 need 260, so there are three words of headroom. The bar was never moved to fit the content; the content was widened and the count raised until the bar held. |

The builder only writes a table entry when its lemma outranks the form's own entry, so a table hit already means the better-ranked reading won. ### `core.cards.probe_cloze --live` — the output, verbatim (production, 2026-08-25)

Reproduced exactly as it was printed. **It exists once and it cost real money** —
14 billed calls, ~792 input tokens each, output 20–183 — and `probe_cloze` writes
nothing by design, so this block is the only durable copy. Re-taking it means 14
more billed calls against rows that no longer exist.

```
  16 · cloze · 'We split the model deployment into three _____s: dev, staging, and production.' · 1 class  ** NOT RECOVERABLE **
  18 · cloze · 'This new model is a _____ above the last version in accuracy.' · 5 classes
  20 · cloze · '_____, the training script caught the error before it crashed the whole pipeline.' · 0 classes  ** NOT RECOVERABLE **
  22 · cloze · 'We used a simple script to _____ the whole environment before running the model.' · 1 class  ** NOT RECOVERABLE **
  24 · cloze · 'We need a _____ validation set before we trust these accuracy numbers.' · 1 class
  26 · cloze · 'The model was _____ of handling inputs longer than its context window.' · 1 class
  28 · cloze · 'The documentary explained how certain drugs can trigger _____ in vulnerable people.' · 5 classes
  30 · cloze · "It's _____ to test the model locally before pushing it to the cloud." · 7 classes  ** NOT RECOVERABLE **
  32 · cloze · 'The constant delays at the airport really started to _____ everyone waiting there.' · 4 classes
  34 · cloze · "There are deposits, utility bills, furniture, and sometimes a broker's fee that can _____ before you even unpack a single box." · 1 class  ** NOT RECOVERABLE **
  36 · cloze · 'She found a cozy studio that seemed, at first glance, _____.' · 0 classes  ** NOT RECOVERABLE **
  38 · cloze · '"I wish someone had warned me to ask about _____ upfront," she said.' · 0 classes  ** NOT RECOVERABLE **
  40 · cloze · 'Her story is common: many renters sign a lease without reading the fine print, then _____ when unexpected charges appear.' · 4 classes  ** NOT RECOVERABLE **
  42 · cloze · 'In the end, choosing an apartment is rarely a simple financial decision... while one that feels cramped or noisy can quietly _____.' · 3 classes  ** NOT RECOVERABLE **

14 cloze cards probed · 6 multi-acceptable · 9 not_recoverable
Prediction was 6-11 multi-acceptable: MET.
Branch: 4-9 -> mixed. B (cue on the face) for the live cards, A (gate at creation) from W10.
9 card(s) are not answerable as authored — a stronger defect than ambiguity, with a different fix. Listed above.
```

**Three things are readable here that are not readable in the summary line, and
each of them changed something above.**

**1. The card that motivated the entire investigation returned NO answer at all.**
`probe_cloze`'s own docstring opens with card 38 — *"I wish someone had warned me
to ask about _____ upfront," she said.* — and states that *hidden costs*, *the
price*, *fees* and *the terms* all fit, so the learner cannot know which is
wanted. **The model offered zero candidates.** The founding example of
*multi-acceptable* is in fact `0 classes` / `not_recoverable`. That reading was a
person's, and it was reasonable; it was never a measurement, and the measurement
disagrees. **This is the axis lesson in one card**: the whole probe was built to
count answer classes because one card looked ambiguous to a human, and that card
had a different defect.

**2. `1 class` and `NOT RECOVERABLE` together is the signature of the substring
bug and of the phrase gap** — cards 16, 22 and 34. The model produced exactly one
confident answer and it was not the card's own. On 16 that is `_____s:` inviting
a singular noun; on 34 an entire clause (*add up*) is missing from a
seventy-word sentence. **Neither is ambiguity. A cue on the face — the branch the
module recommended — would have made both worse**, by adding a first letter to a
slot whose problem is that it is the wrong size.

**3. The work bias is 7 of 14, not 6.** Cards **16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26 and 30**
are model-and-deploy framed: *model deployment · dev, staging, production ·
accuracy · training script · pipeline · script · environment · validation set ·
context window · test the model locally · pushing to the cloud*. **Exactly 50%,
against §4's 20% cap.** The handover counted six and did not count **card 22**
(*"We used a simple script to _____ the whole environment before running the
model"*) — found only by reading the verbatim lines rather than the summary. The
ids are listed so the count is re-checkable by someone who was not there, which
is the whole reason this block is here. The remaining seven are one documentary
sentence, one airport sentence and five about renting a flat.

## Known issues

| # | Issue | Severity | Slice | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 181 | **A slang card has no lemma this schema can express, so 15 recognition cards keep `lexeme_id` NULL and stay outside every lemma-keyed guarantee.** The consequence of #180's fix rather than a separate defect, filed so it is a deferral with an owner. `lexemes` has `lemma`, `pos`, `freq_rank`, `cefr` and `origin` — **and nothing that distinguishes a SENSE.** A slang card teaching *mid* and a seed row meaning *middle* are the same lemma and the same part of speech, and the card is about the difference. So W8f's backfill reaches only `vocabulary`-sourced chunks, and slang cards are invisible to `cards_one_card_per_lemma` and to the capture anti-join. **What that costs today: nothing** — the importer writes single dictionary words and cannot collide with a slang phrase. **What it costs at W13:** tapping *mid* in a transcript cannot tell whether the deck already teaches that sense. **The answer is not a lexemes column bolted on in passing** — it is what identity means for a register-bearing card, which is W13's to design alongside its register detection. **Separately: `delulu` and `low-key` are absent from the seed list, so any pass that resolved them would GROW THE SHARED DICTIONARY** — `lexemes` is global, one row serves every learner — **and whether slang belongs in it is a product decision nobody has made.** | medium | W8f → W13 | ⬜ open — the 11 phrase backs stay NULL permanently and are NOT part of this; that is already ruled |
| 180 | **`mid` identity-matches a seed lexeme meaning *middle*, and the card teaches the slang sense. THE FIFTH APPEARANCE OF THE PATTERN, AND THE FIRST WHERE THE GUARANTEE MATCHES CONFIDENTLY AND WRONGLY.** Found by the **first production dry run of W8f's backfill**, before `--apply`. `mid` resolves by **identity** to `mid` ADJ, **rank 8,955** — a real seed row, an exact string match, nothing invented, no suffix rule involved. **#177's `ti` came through `lemmatize`'s SUFFIX step, so refusing that step fixed it. This arrives through the IDENTITY step, which is the step that was supposed to be the safe one — so neither existing guard sees it.** The consequence is #177's exactly: `013_cards.sql:88` says `lexeme_id` is what `grade_card` writes the ledger from, so the card would have written evidence for *middle* every time a learner graded the slang meaning — into the structure CLAUDE.md §5 calls unrebuildable. **The root cause is that `lexemes` carries `pos` and NO SENSE DISTINCTION**, so *mid*-the-slang and *mid*-the-adjective are one row and the card is about the difference. **Why this one matters more than the previous four:** the earlier cases were predicates that could not MATCH the rows they were about — blindness, which a count exposes. This one matches, confidently, and returns the wrong answer, and **no count anywhere would look wrong.** The only thing that surfaced it was a human reading a printed resolution path for a row nobody had asked about. **The check that catches this family is asking what a predicate cannot match; the check that catches THIS is asking whether a match means what it says.** | medium | W8f → W13 | ✅ **closed 2026-08-26 for W8f's own path, and confirmed on production**: the backfill touched **ids 17–33 only** — the nine vocabulary rows — and no slang card gained a `lexeme_id`. `cards_needing_a_lexeme` reaches only `vocabulary`-sourced chunks and `test_a_slang_card_is_out_of_reach_of_the_backfill` holds it. **The underlying gap is #181 and stays open**: nothing prevents a future pass from making the same match |
| 178 | **The capture path has no "already saved" answer, so `cards_one_card_per_lemma` raises where a route must refuse politely.** W8f's index is the right guarantee and a `UniqueViolation` is the right outcome for a human-run command that prints it. Through `POST /video/{id}/save-word` (ARCHITECTURE §6) it is a **500 for a learner who tapped a word they had already saved** — which is not an error, it is the normal case on a second viewing. The importer avoids it with a row-level anti-join; a route needs an *already saved* response distinct from a failure, and the shape of that answer is W13's to choose. **Filed now so the route meets a known constraint rather than a 500 in front of a learner.** | medium | W8f → W13 | ⬜ open |
| 177 | **`lemmatize` resolves `tier` to `ti`, and the same shape reaches anything absent from the 15,000-lemma seed list.** `tier` is not a known lemma, so step 3's suffix rules strip `-er`, propose `['ti','tie']`, and `ti` **is** in the seed list at rank 9,856 — an OpenSubtitles artefact — so the guard *"a candidate is accepted only if it is already a known lemma"* passes. The docstring's *"it can fail to resolve, but it cannot invent"* holds **literally** and fails **in effect**. **This is live today and is not W8f's defect:** `core.lexicon.coverage` calls `lemmatize` on every transcript token, so `tier` in any text already counts as `ti`, and **PRD §7.2 selects videos on that coverage number** — which is why W12 is the target. W8f routes around it (`resolve_capture_lemma` never calls it) and deliberately does **not** fix it: changing the lemmatiser moves **every coverage figure this project has recorded**, and that is its own slice with its own before-and-after. `tests/test_cards_import_vocab.py` pins `lemmatize("tier") == "ti"` so a future fix explains why that file exists. | medium | W4 → W12 | ⬜ open |
| 176 | **`migrate_chunks` created 14 cards with no `lexeme_id`, so every lemma-keyed guarantee was blind to the whole deck.** The string `lexeme` does not occur in that module: its spec is built from a `common` dict with no such key, so `create_card`'s `None` default applied, and `source_chunk_id` is set on every branch. (a) The skip is row-level by ruling, so a word with a production card does not gain a recognition card — W13 owns whether a partially-carded word is topped up. (b) **Rarity is recorded but nothing acts on it:** D2 ships no frequency floor, so a rank-14,342 capture becomes a card like any other, and nothing deprioritises it in scheduling. `freq_rank` is on `lexemes` and the card reaches it through `lexeme_id`, so the input exists. | 171 | **SEQUENCING: W10 must not be PLANNED until #164 is settled, and this is filed as a blocker in its own right because #164's escalation clause named only W9.** **W10 generates items against each unit's `grammar_targets` and the Murphy citations attached to them** — the exact surface #164's clause names, *"it escalates to `high` on the first slice that shows a Murphy citation to a learner"*. That clause was written with W9's skill map in view; **W10 is a second such slice, and generation is the worse of the two** — a skill map renders a citation the learner can compare against the book in one glance, whereas **a generated item embeds the citation's assumption in the item itself**, where being wrong is not visible at all. **The three contradictions, which need no book to establish:** **Murphy 19–20** cited by **unit 3** for *used to for habits that have stopped* and by **unit 9** for *present continuous for arrangements* — six weeks and two stages apart, sent to the same two pages; **Murphy 38** cited by **unit 12** for *must and can't* and by **unit 17** for *third conditional*. One book unit cannot teach both members of either pair. **WHY IT BLOCKS PLANNING AND NOT JUST SHIPPING: a wrong citation fails SILENTLY.** The learner assumes the book is correct, finds the pages do not match what the week is asking of them, and **concludes they are confused** — so nothing surfaces as a defect and the damage is to the learner's confidence rather than to the output. ### S4c off-site destination options

Set in `.env` (directory must already exist and be writable — the script never creates it):

```
BACKUP_OFFSITE_DIR=/absolute/path/to/existing/folder
```

1. **Cloud-synced folder** (zero-credential on this Mac) — iCloud Drive / Dropbox / Google Drive desktop. Script writes a file; the sync client moves it off-machine.
   - **iCloud:** turn off "Optimise Mac Storage" for that folder/machine, or expect `.english_bot_*.dump.icloud` placeholders. Freshness and retention treat placeholders as present (healthy). Dropbox / Google Drive have equivalent selective-sync / online-only behaviour.
2. **`rsync`** to a second host (Hetzner-era): e.g. `rsync -av ~/english-bot-backups/ user@offsite:/path/`.
3. **`rclone`** to object storage (Hetzner-era): e.g. `rclone copy ~/english-bot-backups remote:bucket/`.

No cloud SDK or credentials live in this repo.

### S15a watched-folder layout

Set in `.env` (directory must already exist outside the repo — bot never invents a Drive mount):

```
WATCH_DIR=/absolute/path/to/existing/folder
```

Auto-created under `WATCH_DIR` for each registered user:

```
inbox/<telegram_user_id>/
  trancy/
  language_reactor/
outbox/<telegram_user_id>/
processed/<telegram_user_id>/
failed/<telegram_user_id>/
```

On this Mac: point at a Google Drive–synced folder (no credentials). **On Hetzner prod: `WATCH_DIR` deliberately unset** — no Drive client; S15a dormant; CSV via Telegram (S15b) only. `rclone` + Google service account remains an open option if the folder bridge is ever needed on the server.

**Operator logs (S18 / prod):** `journalctl -u english-bot -f` (preferred on Hetzner); also `tail -f /home/bot/english-bot-runtime/bot.log`. Message content never appears in either.

## Verification checklist

Do not start S9b until these are cleared or explicitly deferred.

### How to verify

1. Start the bot: `.venv/bin/python -m app.main`
2. Watch the terminal alongside Telegram.
3. Tail the rotating log: `tail -f ~/english-bot-runtime/bot.log`

was RUN and not assumed: 1762 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failing**, against W8e's
baseline of 1685 — 77 new tests, and the one failure that appeared along the way
was `test_record_consistency`'s own guard refusing a migration with no

**Two of the three human checks are RUN and the two that matter most are not.**
The importer's behaviour is now observed on production — the backfill split
`7 identity + 2 grown` exactly as predicted, the Trancy re-import wrote **0** of
9, and a second `--apply` wrote nothing. **What is unrun is the half no command
can answer: nobody has looked at one of these cards on a phone**, and `swain` —
rank 11,886, from an 18th-century autobiography — is now in a 33-card deck on the
strength of a ruling that has never met a screen.

**#27 CLOSES, and it closes with the defect MEASURED instead of described.** A
real Language Reactor export is committed as a fixture, and the v2 path reading it
produces **7 headers and 9 phantom rows from a 2-record, 24-column file**, then
refuses it. Three causes, all in the file: **no header row at all**, **tab**
separation, and **literal newlines inside quoted fields**. A real LR export has
never been importable since S15a. **Both halves are asserted** — the refusal and
the fix — so it cannot silently reopen.

**THE SLICE'S OWN FOUNDING DEFECT, and it was found in review rather than by any
gate.** `migrate_chunks` sets `source_chunk_id` on every card and `lexeme_id` on
none, so the duplicate guarantee as first drafted matched **zero of the 14
production cards**. Run as written, the step described as *the duplicate test*
would have reported 9 imported instead of 9 skipped and written **a second `tier`
card beside card 17**. Corrected by keying identity on the **lemma** and by
`core.cards.backfill_lexemes` (#176). **A second, sharper trap was found and
routed around, not fixed:** `lemmatize("tier")` returns **`ti`** — a real seed row
at rank 9,856 — so a backfill through the lemmatiser would have pointed card 17 at
the wrong word and corrupted the ledger on every grade, **and it would have read
green**, because the importer makes the identical error on the identical input
(#177, filed against W4 → W12 and deliberately not fixed here).

**S24a'S RECORD IS CORRECTED.** Its row reads `9 words → 8 imported / 1 skipped
(frustrate)`. The committed fixture is **byte-identical** to
`VOCABULARY LIST 2026-08-14.csv`, contains nine rows **including `frustrate`**,
the census counts nine `vocabulary` chunks, and `frustrate` is the back of card
32. **There was one import, of nine rows, and the reply's count was wrong** —
neither "a second import ran" nor "the skip did not skip".

**Two rulings, with their authorship, because the distinction cannot be
reconstructed later.** The LR-over-Trancy ruling and the cards-directly creator
are **assistant-recommended, operator-accepted**. **The dropped frequency floor is
assistant-proposed, assistant-reviewed-against, operator-accepted** — the
objection came from the reviewing assistant, not from the operator, and the losing
argument is kept in the decisions log because the threshold will look
re-proposable to the next reader.

**THE PRODUCTION DRY RUN WAS RUN AND STOPPED BEFORE `--apply`. It found two
things, and both are folded in above rather than left as deploy-time surprises.**
(1) The `tier` provenance query compared `meaning` to the **Translation column
alone** and returned `f`; the stored value is `btrim(Translation) || ' (' ||
Phonetic || ')'`, so **the claim is stronger than it was written** — two columns
from one Trancy row through `format_meaning`, whose source is in this repository.
(2) **`mid` identity-matched a seed lexeme meaning *middle* (#180)**, so the
backfill is narrowed to `vocabulary`-sourced chunks and step 9's expected split is
the predicted `7 identity + 2 grown`.

**THE PATTERN REACHES ITS FIFTH APPEARANCE, AND #180 IS NOT THE SAME FAILURE AS
THE OTHER FOUR.** Those were guarantees evaluated against a set that **could not
contain** the thing they were about — blindness, which a count exposes. **`mid`
matches, confidently, and is wrong, and no count anywhere would have looked
wrong**: the split would have read `identity 8 + grown 2` and every total would
have reconciled. **What surfaced it was a human reading a printed resolution PATH
for a row nobody had asked about** — the second time in this slice that printing
the path rather than the total is what caught a defect. So: **the deploy steps
below read split counts and named words, never totals, and a bare `9` is not
evidence.** The check that catches the first four is asking what a predicate
CANNOT match; the check that catches this one is asking whether a match MEANS what
it says — and that question has no mechanical form here, because `lexemes` cannot
express the distinction the answer depends on (#181).

correction before them, and W8c — and **the record's own sentence about them was

holding.** It is held now, and **W8c's lesson repeated exactly: it exists because
a person looked at a screen, and this is a person looking at content.**

**THE FINDING, and it is not the one check A anticipated.** **The 24 can-dos are
GRAMMAR, not topics.** Units 1–17 are Murphy targets with a sentence wrapped
round them — present perfect, past perfect, comparatives, articles, conditionals,
passive, reported speech — and **a grammar unit has no vocabulary field, so its
65 lexemes have no reason to be those 65.** Unit 2's can-do is *"I can say
whether I've done something before, and when"* and its words include `sausage,
puppy, hammer, widow, traitor`: **those words are not in the wrong unit; there is
no right unit for them.**

**Unit 9 looked correctly tagged and that was coincidence.** Its grammar is about
the future, so `postpone, reservation, reminder, arrangement, standby` fit by
accident of subject matter rather than by tagging — **a reading that had sampled
unit 9 alone would have gone into this record as a pass**, which is the argument
for three units rather than one.

**The only units with a real topic are 18–21** — work, price and terms, email,
collocations — **and their lists are genuinely coherent**: `supplier, brand,
accountant, corporation, investor`. **The tagger worked exactly where a topic
existed to tag against, and nowhere else.**

**This is the unit-vs-stage granularity problem one level deeper than this record
has had it.** W8 already found that the lexical field is a property of the STAGE
and that grammar has no vocabulary, and fixed it by assigning a stage and
splitting deterministically across four units. **That treats the problem as
granularity. It is not: it is a grammar spine and a vocabulary spine joined as
though they were one thing.** **Filed as #161, with the ruling it owes.**

**Two evidenced positives, recorded because they close questions.** **The grammar
spine is good** — the 24 can-dos read in order as a real B1→B2 progression, so
**this is not a finding that W8's content is bad.** And **Work is 4 of 24 units,

4. **Open Murphy at three cited units and confirm the grammar target matches.**
   **PART-RUN 2026-08-26 AND BLOCKED ON THE BOOK — recorded as blocked, not
   carried.** **The operator does not have Murphy to hand and verifies tonight.**
   **The half that needed no book is DONE and it found a defect: the citations
   contradict each other** (**#164**). Unit 12 cites `38` for *must and can't*;
   unit 17 cites `38-39` for *third conditional*; **one book unit cannot teach
   both.** A query over all 24 units says the set is **closed at three** —
   **Murphy 19, 20 and 38** — out of 36 numbers cited more than once, **the other
   33 being a broad target citing the span its narrow siblings partition inside
   one unit, which is authored structure and not a defect.** **A constant edition
   offset cannot explain the three**, because a uniform shift maps equal numbers
   to equal numbers, **so the collisions and the edition question are separate
   and only the second needs the book to exist.**

   **The query, so the count is re-checkable and not an assertion** — it reads
   the committed data and writes nothing:

   ```bash
   cd /home/bot/english-bot && .venv/bin/python -c "
   import json, re, collections
   u = json.load(open('data/syllabus_units.json'))
   def ex(sp):
       out = []
       for part in str(sp).split(','):
           m = re.match(r'^(\d+)\s*-\s*(\d+)$', part.strip())
           out.extend(range(int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)) + 1) if m else [int(part.strip())])
       return out
   idx = collections.defaultdict(list)
   for x in u:
       for t in x['grammar_targets']:
           for m in ex(t['murphy_units']) if t.get('murphy_units') else []:
               idx[m].append((x['unit_number'], t['target'], t['murphy_units']))
   for m in sorted(idx):
       if len({c[0] for c in idx[m]}) > 1:
           print('Murphy', m, '<-', sorted({c[0] for c in idx[m]}))
           for un, tg, sp in idx[m]: print('   unit', un, '|', tg, '|', sp)"
   ```

     perfect: the thing that happened first*.
   - **Does 38 teach must/can't?** If it does, **unit 17's third conditional is
     the wrong citation**; if it teaches the third conditional, **unit 12's three
     citations are.** One of the two clusters is wrong and the book says which.
   - **Do 36-37 teach might/may/could?** Unit 12 cites them for *might, may and
     could for possibility*, and they sit beside the 38 cluster, so getting them
     right localises the error.
   - **WHICH EDITION were these citations generated against?** **Murphy
     renumbers between the 4th and 5th, and a constant offset would explain a
     whole-set mismatch differently from invented numbers** — the first is one
     scripted correction over 69 citations, the second is 69 hand-checks. **The
     data cannot tell them apart and the book can.**

   **Why its weight rose this morning and was paid this afternoon: check A found
   the grammar spine to be the good half and the load-bearing half** — if the

## Superseded — the W8e Next action preamble, kept for the record

**Superseded by W8f on 2026-08-26. Kept verbatim rather than edited**, because
its stop-conditions and its two rulings are the record of what was decided, and
a preamble rewritten in place cannot be told from one that was never written.


**W8e is RECORDS ONLY and 🟡. Two W10 rulings and one sequencing constraint were
recorded; nothing else happened.** **No code, no migration, no server step** —
`schema_version` stays at **14**, no `.sql` file added or edited, no
`packages/core` change. **The suite was RUN and not assumed: 1685 passed / 6
skipped / 0 failing in 107s, Vitest 74 across 7 files — identical to W8d.** **Nothing on the check list below is closed by
this slice and nothing on it is carried silently.**

**RULING 1 — #157 is ruled and SPLIT BY CARD TYPE.** `production` and `cloze`
take a **typed answer**, graded through the seam that already exists —
`equivalence_key` (`grading.py:100`) and `distinct_answers` (`grading.py:127`),
already used by `gates.py` and `probe_cloze.py:183-191` — **and no second
normaliser is added.** **`recognition` keeps W6's reveal-then-self-mark**, and
the exemption is principled: **its answer is a MEANING, and a meaning cannot be
machine-graded against a typed string.** A typed recognition card would grade the
learner's wording rather than their memory and fail them for being right in
different words — §4's no-guilt rule by a different road. **The reason, from
use:** *a card that shows the answer on a tap and then asks the learner to grade
themselves cannot distinguish recall from recognition, and that distinction is
the whole difference between knowing a word and thinking you know it.*
**Recorded explicitly: noticed by the operator USING the reviewer, not by any
gate** — the second time in three slices after W8c. **#157 stays ⬜ open: the
ruling is recorded, W10 executes it.**

**RULING 2 — #170: checkpoints stay PURE GRAMMAR in W10, and #170 moves W11 →
W13.** Do not re-source checkpoint vocabulary from the learner's FSRS due cards;
**W8d's redistribution stands as shipped.** **The trigger is stated as DECK SIZE,
not a date:** the deck is **29 cards** and **W8b removed 14 of them**, so a
due-card source that small either returns nothing or returns the same handful in
every unit, and the empty-deck fallback would run more often than the path it
falls back from. **W13 is named because video capture is what makes the deck
large enough** — if the deck grows another way this is ready earlier; if W13
slips, the condition is still deck size. **Second reason, deck-independent:**
option (b) couples checkpoint content to deck state, and **W10 is the first slice
that generates items at all**, so both defects would arrive together and be
indistinguishable from the output.

**BOTH RULINGS ARE ASSISTANT-RECOMMENDED AND OPERATOR-ACCEPTED**, recorded the
way W8c's five glosses and the #161 ruling were — **the distinction between
authored and accepted is what someone asking "why was this decided" needs, and
it cannot be reconstructed later.**

**THE SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT — #171, new, and filed in its own right: W10 MUST NOT
BE PLANNED until #164 is settled.** **W10 generates items against each unit's
grammar targets and their Murphy citations** — precisely the surface #164's
escalation clause names, *"to `high` on the first slice that shows a Murphy
citation to a learner"*, **a clause written with W9 in view that named one slice
too few.** **Three citations contradict each other, provable with no book:
Murphy 19–20** cited by unit 3 for *used to for habits that have stopped* and by
unit 9 for *present continuous for arrangements*; **Murphy 38** cited by unit 12
for *must and can't* and by unit 17 for *third conditional*. **A wrong citation
FAILS SILENTLY** — the learner assumes the book is correct, finds the pages do
not match the week, **and concludes they are confused** — which is why it blocks
PLANNING and not merely shipping: **a slice cannot design around a fault it will
not be able to see.** **The constraint the record already established, restated
because it is the thing most likely to be forgotten: a uniform edition offset
cannot explain a collision**, since a uniform shift maps equal numbers to equal
numbers — **so the edition question and the contradictions are INDEPENDENT, and
settling the edition does not clear them.** **Filed as its own numbered row
because a constraint that lives only inside another issue's prose is one a
planner reads past.**

**W8 check 4 is the unblocking step and it is unchanged** — **PART-RUN and
blocked on the book**, carried below with **all four questions** so the sitting
is one pass: does Murphy unit **25** teach past perfect · does **38** teach
must/can't · do **36–37** teach might/may/could · **which edition**. **W8 check 2
stays BLOCKED**: it asks whether work vocabulary leaked into units 1–16, and

question is not one that can be true or false.

**Do not start W9. Do not start W10.**

### W8's five content checks — unrun through FIVE slices now, and still the whole question

**They stay first, and this is the fifth time they have been first.** W8r, W8a,
W8b and this post-deploy fold each carried them forward untouched, and a check
carried four times without being run is one the record is describing rather than
holding. **W8 is deployed and nothing in it has been read by a person.** The rows are
correctly shaped, correctly constrained and correctly counted — that is what the
queries prove. Whether 24 weeks of authored content is any good is unmeasured,
and for a content slice that is the whole question. **A criterion of ">=30
lexemes" is satisfied by thirty bad words: the count is machine-checkable and the
quality is not.**

1. **Read three units end to end** — one from stage 1, one from stage 3, one from
   stage 5. Can-do statement, every grammar target, both output tasks, and 20 of
   the target lexemes. **Judge whether a B1 learner would recognise this as a
   week's work.** No test can do this and it is the only check that matters here.

   ```bash
   cd /home/bot/english-bot && .venv/bin/python -c "
   import json; u=json.load(open('data/syllabus_units.json'))
   for n in (2, 11, 19):
       x=u[n-1]; print('=== UNIT', n, '===', x['can_do'])
       for t in x['grammar_targets']: print('  -', t['target'], '|', t['murphy_units'])
       print('  spoken:', x['output_task_spoken']); print('  written:', x['output_task_written'])"
   grep -P "\t(2|11|19)\t" data/syllabus_lexemes.tsv | cut -f1 | tr '\n' ' '
   ```

2. **Read stage 5's lexical field specifically, and check it has not leaked.**
   Units 17–20 are the only work units; CLAUDE.md §4 caps Work at 20% and v2's
   biggest product failure was everything sounding like a Slack message about a
   deploy. **Work vocabulary appearing in units 1–16 is that failure recurring
   inside the syllabus itself.** The sample read looked clean — unit 19 is
   `campaign, agency, bid, quote, proposal, wage, discount, invoice`, and units 1,
   8 and 22 carry none of it — but that is four units of 24. **W8b's 7-of-14
   measurement on the deck is the same failure found in live learner content**,
   which makes this check more urgent rather than less. **2026-08-25 sharpens
   it**: those fourteen came from S24a's sentence generator, which had no track
   weighting at all — the syllabus authoring did, so this check is asking whether
   having the rule was enough.

3. **Read 30 random rows of `data/syllabus_lexemes.tsv` against their unit's
   lexical field and say how many are wrong.** That number goes in the record
   **next to the 69% machine agreement rate** — one measures self-consistency,
   the other correctness, and the record will not confuse them (#137).

   ```bash
   cd /home/bot/english-bot && shuf -n 30 <(grep -v '^#' data/syllabus_lexemes.tsv | tail -n +2) | sort -t$'\t' -k2 -n | awk -F'\t' '{print $2"\t"$1}'
   ```

4. **Open Murphy at three cited units and confirm the grammar target matches.**
   The one check that needs the book, and **nothing in the repository can
   substitute for it**: `book_units` is not a catalogue (#133), so the references
   are validated for format and bounds only. Try unit 1's `5` (past simple), unit
   11's `33-34` (second conditional) and unit 18's `137-139` (phrasal verbs).

5. **Read the four checkpoint blueprints of one stage** and confirm they test the
   unit's targets rather than restating them.

### Deploy — W8b. Run as `bot`. Stop at the first step whose evidence does not match.

**This deploy deletes production rows.** Two steps can stop it: step 1 and step 5.

**Step 1 — status BEFORE anything. This is the step whose mismatch means stop (#141).**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && .venv/bin/python -m core.db status
```

**Evidence:** `Applied: 001–014, Pending: (none)`. Anything else means production
is not where this file claims it is — **stop and do not continue.**

**Step 2 — backup. Mandatory, and not for the usual reason.**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && ./scripts/backup.sh
```

**Evidence:** a new object under `english_bot/2026/08/`, **at least 302,116
bytes**. Every earlier slice took a backup because a migration might fail. **This
one deletes fourteen rows on purpose**, and the backup is the only path back if
the ruling turns out to be wrong.

**Step 3 — pull and install. This must come BEFORE the purge.**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && git pull && .venv/bin/pip install -e packages/core
```

**Evidence:** the commit hash matches what was pushed; `pip` reports
`core-0.1.0`. **No new dependency.**

**Why the order is load-bearing:** purging before this leaves a `migrate_chunks
--apply` able to recreate all fourteen, and it would report `cloze_created 14` as
an ordinary success.

**Step 4 — status AFTER, unchanged**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && .venv/bin/python -m core.db status
```

**Evidence:** `Applied: 001–014, Pending: (none)`, **identical to Step 1.**

**Step 5 — the `card_reviews` check. THE SECOND STOP STEP.**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "SELECT c.id, count(r.id) FROM cards c LEFT JOIN card_reviews r ON r.card_id = c.id WHERE c.card_type = 'cloze' GROUP BY c.id ORDER BY c.id;"
```

**Evidence: 14 rows, every count 0.** W7 recorded `card_reviews` 0 and its five
review checks are still unrun, so it is probably still 0 — but **if any count is
non-zero, stop and report it.** Deleting the card discards a real learner event;
`card_reviews` is append-only by design and cascades from `cards`. **The ruling
assumes these cards have never been reviewed; if that is false the decision
changes and it is not Claude's to re-make.** (`retire_chunk_cloze` refuses on its
own if it sees one — this step is the independent read, run before the command
that would act on it.)

**Step 6 — two read-only censuses, before anything is deleted**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "SELECT source, count(*) FROM chunks GROUP BY source ORDER BY 2 DESC;"
```

**Evidence:** the breakdown, recorded in this file. **If the work-heavy chunks
come from one source, that is worth knowing before W13 imports more of the same**
— and it is the nearest thing to progress on #57, which is not closed by W8b's
fourteen-card sample.

**Step 6b — #147's count, on the cards that are STAYING**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "SELECT count(*) FROM cards WHERE card_type = 'production' AND source_chunk_id IS NOT NULL AND front ~ '_____[a-z]';"
```

**Evidence:** a number, recorded in **#147**. These are surviving production
cards whose context hint was built by the substring gapper — `three _____s:` —
and they are **not** being deleted. **A defect live on cards a learner opens
tomorrow deserves a count, not a description; and if it is zero that is worth
recording too**, because it bounds how often the substring bug actually bites.

**Step 7 — the purge, dry. Paste this output into the record before step 8.**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && .venv/bin/python -m core.cards.retire_chunk_cloze
```

**Evidence:** `14 chunk-derived cloze card(s)`, every row printed with its front
and `0 reviews`, ending `dry run — nothing was deleted`. **If the count is not
14, that is itself the finding — record it and stop.**
**This output is the last record of those fourteen sentences.** After step 8 they
exist nowhere.

**Step 8 — the purge**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && .venv/bin/python -m core.cards.retire_chunk_cloze --purge
```

Type `14` when asked. **Evidence:** `deleted 14 card(s)` with the ids listed. Any
`FINDING:` line means a review landed between the read and the write — **that is
not a successful run; record it.**

**Step 9 — the independent verification. In psql, not from the command that did the work.**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "SELECT count(*) FROM cards;" -c "SELECT count(*) FROM cards WHERE card_type = 'cloze';" -c "SELECT count(*) FROM chunks;" -c "SELECT card_type, count(*) FROM cards GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;"
```

**Evidence:** `cards` **29** · `cloze` **0** · `chunks` **29** · breakdown
`production 14`, `recognition 15`. §3 rule 5: a count the deleting command prints
about its own work is not verification of it.

**Step 10 — run it again**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && .venv/bin/python -m core.cards.retire_chunk_cloze
```

**Evidence:** `0 chunk-derived cloze card(s)` and `Nothing to do.`

**Step 11 — restart `english-api` only. `english-bot` is deliberately left running.**

```bash
exit   # back to root
systemctl restart english-api && systemctl status english-api --no-pager | head -5
```

**Evidence:** `active (running)`.

**Why the bot is not restarted**, stated again because omitting it would read as
an oversight: nothing it imports changed in behaviour — `core/services/anki.py`
is byte-identical, the new service functions are additive, and `core/cards/`'s
constants have no bot reader. PTB polls with `drop_pending_updates=True`, so a
restart silently discards whatever a learner sent in that window and they get no
reply and no error. CLAUDE.md §5b's reasoning applied to a restart.

**Do not touch Caddy or PostgreSQL** — the host is shared with `fonderis-worker`.

### W8's five content checks — unrun through four slices, and still the whole question

**W8 is deployed and nothing in it has been read by a person.** The rows are
correctly shaped, correctly constrained and correctly counted — that is what the
queries prove. Whether 24 weeks of authored content is any good is unmeasured,
and for a content slice that is the whole question. **A criterion of ">=30
lexemes" is satisfied by thirty bad words: the count is machine-checkable and the
quality is not.**

1. **Read three units end to end** — one from stage 1, one from stage 3, one from
   stage 5. Can-do statement, every grammar target, both output tasks, and 20 of
   the target lexemes. **Judge whether a B1 learner would recognise this as a
   week's work.** No test can do this and it is the only check that matters here.

   ```bash
   cd /home/bot/english-bot && .venv/bin/python -c "
   import json; u=json.load(open('data/syllabus_units.json'))
   for n in (2, 11, 19):
       x=u[n-1]; print('=== UNIT', n, '===', x['can_do'])
       for t in x['grammar_targets']: print('  -', t['target'], '|', t['murphy_units'])
       print('  spoken:', x['output_task_spoken']); print('  written:', x['output_task_written'])"
   grep -P "\t(2|11|19)\t" data/syllabus_lexemes.tsv | cut -f1 | tr '\n' ' '
   ```

2. **Read stage 5's lexical field specifically, and check it has not leaked.**
   Units 17–20 are the only work units; CLAUDE.md §4 caps Work at 20% and v2's
   biggest product failure was everything sounding like a Slack message about a
   deploy. **Work vocabulary appearing in units 1–16 is that failure recurring
   inside the syllabus itself.** The sample read looked clean — unit 19 is
   `campaign, agency, bid, quote, proposal, wage, discount, invoice`, and units 1,

### Deploy — W8

Run as `bot` on the production host, in order. Stop at the first step whose
evidence does not match.

**Step 1 — pre-flight, because step 4's foreign key depends on it**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "SELECT count(*) FROM items WHERE unit_number IS NOT NULL;"
```

**Evidence:** `0`. #109 closed with `items` at 0 and W7 created cards, not items,
so this should still hold. **If it is not 0, do not continue** — 014 adds
`items_unit_number_fkey` as `NOT VALID` precisely so the migration cannot fail
here, but a non-zero count means rows exist that the seed's `VALIDATE` in step 5
will reject, and it is better to know now.

**Step 2 — backup, mandatory before every migration**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && ./scripts/backup.sh
```

**Evidence:** a new object in R2 under `english_bot/2026/08/`, **at least
287,649 bytes** — that was W7's, and 013's two tables are in this one too, so a
smaller file means something is wrong with the dump, not with the database.

**Step 3 — pull and install**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && git pull && .venv/bin/pip install -e packages/core
```

**Evidence:** the commit hash matches what was pushed, and `pip` reports
`core-0.1.0`. **No new dependency** — W8 adds none, and `core.syllabus` is a new
package inside the one already installed.

**Step 4 — migrate**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && .venv/bin/python -m core.db migrate && .venv/bin/python -m core.db status
```

**Evidence:** `Applied migration 014`, then **`Applied: 001–014, Pending:
(none)`**. On the Mac this took well under a second; the three tables are empty
and the one `ALTER TABLE` is `NOT VALID`, so there is no table scan.

**Step 5 — seed the syllabus. This is the step that is new.**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && .venv/bin/python -m core.syllabus.seed --dry-run
```

**Evidence:** `content ok: 24 units, 1560 candidate lexemes, min 65 per unit
(target 65)` and `dry run — nothing written`. The dry run validates both content
files and checks every candidate resolves to a real `lexemes` row **before**
anything is written; if a lemma is missing it names it and exits 1.

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && .venv/bin/python -m core.syllabus.seed
```

**Evidence, all four lines:**

```
syllabus_units: 24 inserted, 0 updated, 0 unchanged, 0 deleted
syllabus_unit_lexemes: 1560 inserted, 0 updated, 0 unchanged, 0 deleted
orphan candidate rows: 0 (must be 0)
items_unit_number_fkey convalidated: True
```

**`convalidated: True` is an acceptance criterion, not a log line.** 014 adds
that foreign key `NOT VALID` because `syllabus_units` is empty at migration time;
a `NOT VALID` constraint nobody ever validates is a silent hole, and this is the
step that closes it.

**Step 6 — run it again. The second run is the acceptance criterion.**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && .venv/bin/python -m core.syllabus.seed
```

**Evidence:** `0 inserted, 0 updated, 24 unchanged, 0 deleted` and `0 inserted,
0 updated, 1560 unchanged, 0 deleted`. Running this **on production and not only
on the Mac** is what makes it mean anything — W4 established that, and the Mac's
database is not the one with two years of journal in it.

**Step 7 — the per-learner numbers, which is the real acceptance criterion**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && .venv/bin/python -m core.syllabus.seed --report
```

**Evidence:** one line per learner, and **no `BELOW 30` on any of them**. Expect
`min 62-65` for all three: the diff removes only lemmas a learner already has at
`known` or `mastered` **above rank 2000**, and post-#91 the heaviest learner has
exactly three of those. `1`, `2` and `3` are Navid, Morkyte and Amirhossein.
**Read the `min`, not just the absence of a warning** — the criterion is
">=30 target lexemes **per learner, after the diff**", and this is the only place
that number exists.

**Step 8 — an independent count, not the seeder reporting on itself**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "SELECT count(*) FROM syllabus_units; SELECT count(*) FROM syllabus_unit_lexemes; SELECT min(n), max(n) FROM (SELECT count(*) n FROM syllabus_unit_lexemes GROUP BY unit_number) t; SELECT count(*) FROM syllabus_unit_lexemes s LEFT JOIN lexemes l ON l.id = s.lexeme_id WHERE l.id IS NULL;"
```

**Evidence:** `24`, `1560`, `65 | 65`, `0`. Run separately from the command that
did the work, per CLAUDE.md §3 rule 5.

**Step 9 — restart**

```bash
sudo systemctl restart english-bot english-api && systemctl is-active english-bot english-api
```

**Evidence:** `active` twice. **No Vercel deploy is needed** — W8 ships no
frontend and `apps/web` is unchanged.

## Superseded — the W7 Next action, kept for the record

**Every step below ran on 2026-08-25 and none of them is to be run again.** The
outcome is in the W7 slice row and the decisions log. Kept because the branch
rules written *before* the run — step 6's #117 rule in particular — are only
worth having if the version that was written in advance stays readable.

**Its opening paragraph was wrong by the time anyone read it**, and that is the
defect this change exists to fix; it is preserved verbatim rather than edited:

> **W7 is code-complete and NOT deployed.** Migration **013** is applied to the
> Mac dev database only; production is still at **12**. Suite **1381 → 1541
> passing / 6 skipped / 0 failing**; **Vitest 52 → 62**; `pnpm tsc --noEmit`
> clean. Every server step below is a command for the human — **Claude Code has
> no SSH access to this host and is not to be given any**, so no acceptance
> criterion of this slice is one Claude Code could satisfy on its own.

### What landed, and what it rests on

**The deck exists.** `cards` carries the card and its FSRS state; `card_reviews`
is the append-only log. `core/cards/fsrs.py` is the only door to py-fsrs and
reproduces **both of the library's own published test vectors exactly** — the
interval sequence `[0, 2, 11, 46, 163, 498, 0, 0, 2, 4, 7, 12, 21]` and the
memory state `(53.62691, 6.3574867)` — which is the strongest available evidence
that the wrapper is faithful, and it comes from outside our code.

**Three things in the record turned out to be wrong and are corrected rather
than worked around:**

1. **There is no v2 review *history*.** No table logs an individual chunk
   review; `migrations/004_chunk_review.sql` added four aggregate columns and
   that is the whole input. The seeding mapping says so out loud, is versioned,
   and **a chunk with no graded review produces a NULL stability** rather than a
   plausible number.
2. **#100 undercounted its own drift** — seven stale Build columns, not three.
3. **#108's premise is wrong**: FSRS-6 reads no latency in any branch, so W7's
   reviewer schedules on nothing the browser reported.

**And a fourth, from the census itself**: 013's receptive-first CHECK barred
slang `production` cards and permitted slang **`cloze`** cards — a cloze asks
the learner to produce the phrase into a gap, so the rule was broken through the
constraint written to hold it. All three productive types are now barred.
Harmless until the census showed two learners whose whole corpus is slang, at
which point it would have been their entire deck.

**And `chunks` is never modified**, by any part of this slice, asserted by a test
over the migration module's own AST. Together with `seed_basis` — the four v2
numbers copied verbatim onto every seeded card — that is what makes a wrong
mapping an UPDATE with a formula rather than a reconstruction from nothing.

---

### Step 0 — the census. **RUN 2026-08-25, and it stopped the slice.**

```
Navid         5 chunks / 5 slang / 0 with history
Morkyte       5 chunks / 5 slang / 0 with history
Amirhossein  19 chunks / 5 slang / 3 with history
sources: slang 15 · vocabulary 9 · reading_1 5
no chunk lacks a sentence or a meaning
```

**Two findings, and the first one stopped the rehearsal before it started.**

1. **Two of three learners' entire v2 corpus is the S24 slang fan-out.** Under
   the originally-approved ruling — skip slang — Navid and Morkyte got **zero
   cards each**, and acceptance criterion 1 ("the deck is non-empty on day one")
   failed for two learners out of three, on the verification query's own
   "cards > 0 for **each** learner" wording. **The criterion was not adjusted.
   The migration was**: see step 0b.
2. **`with_history` is 3 across the whole database.** The seeding branch fires
   on at most 3 of 29 chunks, so 26 chunks produce genuinely new FSRS cards with
   a NULL stability. The mapping is correct and is kept; the record now carries
   the number (#131) instead of implying a corpus that does not exist.

One caveat on the census's last line: *no chunk lacks a sentence* answers "has a
sentence", not "the phrase is locatable in it". `make_sentence_with_gap` can
still fail — v2's own `due_chunks` logs `chunk_not_in_sentence` skips — so
`production_only_no_gap` is still possible and the dry run is what reports it.

**Two queries still outstanding**, both read-only, both one line:

```bash
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "SELECT u.name, c.source, count(*) AS chunks, count(*) FILTER (WHERE c.times_right + c.times_wrong > 0) AS with_history FROM chunks c JOIN users u ON u.id = c.user_id GROUP BY u.name, c.source ORDER BY u.name, c.source;"
```
**Closes #131** — it says whether the 3 with-history chunks are slang (seeded
cards = 0) or not (seeded cards ≤ 6). Record the answer in that row.

```bash
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "SELECT chunk, count(*) AS rows, count(DISTINCT user_id) AS learners FROM chunks WHERE source = 'slang' GROUP BY chunk ORDER BY 2 DESC;"
```
**Sizes step 0b.** If the 15 slang rows are 5 distinct phrases fanned out to 3
learners, you write five lines, not fifteen.

### Step 0b — write the slang glosses. **This is the step that makes the deck non-empty.**

PRD §8.5.4 requires four things on every slang card. A v2 chunk carries the line
it came from and the meaning; **you supply the neutral equivalent and
who-says-this.** Not a model call, and PRD §8.5.3 would have permitted one — at
five phrases a person who knows these two learners writes better lines than a
model does, and W13 generates them from the real transcript line later.

Generate a template with the phrases already filled in:

```bash
{ printf 'chunk\tneutral_equivalent\twho_says_this\n'; psql "$DATABASE_URL" -At -F$'\t' -c "SELECT DISTINCT chunk, '', '' FROM chunks WHERE source = 'slang' ORDER BY 1;"; } > ~/w7-slang-glosses.tsv
```

`printf` and not `sed '1i …'`: BSD sed refuses that form, so the sed version
works on the server and fails on the Mac. **Verified on 2026-08-25** against the
dev database — it emits the header and one row per distinct slang phrase with
columns 2 and 3 empty, and the reader refuses that unfilled template by line
number until you have written them.

Then fill columns 2 and 3. Three tab-separated columns, a header row, `#`
comments allowed:

```
chunk	neutral_equivalent	who_says_this
hard pass	I'd rather not, thanks	Friends and casual colleagues. Fine in Slack, not in a client email.
```

**The file is never committed** — it is learner shared-library content, and
`data/` holds reference data. **A phrase you leave blank is refused**, not
half-imported: the reader rejects the whole file rather than shipping a slang
card with no safe alternative. **A phrase you leave out entirely** is skipped and
counted in `skipped_slang_no_gloss`, so the bucket table tells you exactly what
is still unwritten.

### Step 5 — the independent verification query

**Typed by hand, sharing no code with the migration** (CLAUDE.md §3 rule 5, and
W4b's precedent). Run on the scratch copy in step 1 and again here; paste both
outputs into this file.

```bash
psql "$DATABASE_URL" <<'SQL'
SELECT u.id, u.name,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM chunks k WHERE k.user_id = u.id) AS chunks,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE c.card_type = 'cloze')      AS cloze,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE c.card_type = 'production') AS production,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE c.seeded_from_history)      AS seeded,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT c.seeded_from_history)  AS fresh
  FROM users u LEFT JOIN cards c ON c.user_id = u.id
 GROUP BY u.id, u.name ORDER BY u.id;

SELECT 'untagged'          AS check, count(*) FROM cards WHERE register IS NULL
UNION ALL SELECT 'review state without parameters', count(*) FROM cards
   WHERE fsrs_state <> 'learning' AND (stability IS NULL OR difficulty IS NULL)
UNION ALL SELECT 'seeded without a basis', count(*) FROM cards
   WHERE seeded_from_history AND seed_basis = '{}'::jsonb
UNION ALL SELECT 'orphan source_chunk_id', count(*) FROM cards c
   LEFT JOIN chunks k ON k.id = c.source_chunk_id
   WHERE c.source_chunk_id IS NOT NULL AND k.id IS NULL
UNION ALL SELECT 'fabricated review events', count(*) FROM card_reviews;

SELECT is_nullable, column_default FROM information_schema.columns
 WHERE table_name = 'cards' AND column_name = 'register';
SQL
```

**Expected evidence:** cards **> 0 for each learner**, not merely in total —
**this is the assertion the census broke, so read all three rows**; every
row of the second block **0**; and the third returning `NO` with a **NULL**
default — a count of zero untagged rows would prove nothing on a small table,
and the absence of a default is what makes an untagged card unexpressible.

## Superseded — the W5b Next action, kept for the record

**W5b is an investigation. It fixes nothing, and that is the deliverable.** No
migration, no API change, no frontend change, no server step, no `packages/core`
change to any existing file. **`schema_version` stays at 12**; 013 belongs to W7.
Suite **1340 → 1366 passing / 6 skipped / 0 failing**; **Vitest 52**, unchanged.
`git diff --stat` is **empty** — the slice is two new files.

### What the tree already answered, before a call was billed

**#115 was a false dichotomy and both of its branches are wrong.** The gate hands
`judge_naturalness` the string `checks.sentence_of(item)` returns, which for
`mcq`, `cloze_cued` and `collocation_pick` is the **gapped stem** and for
`error_spot` is **the sentence with its deliberate error still in it**. The
prompt asks *"would a real person say this to a friend?"*, never mentions gaps or
exercises, and instructs the model to reject anything *"nobody actually phrases
that way"*. **A model that rejects `"I ___ to the shops yesterday."` is obeying
that instruction correctly.**

The dry run prints the partition and it is perfect, eleven of eleven:

```
mcq                    A: 'I ___ to the shops yesterday.'  <-- GAPPED/ERRORED
cloze_cued             A: 'I ___ to the shops yesterday.'  <-- GAPPED/ERRORED
error_spot             A: 'I goed to the shops'            <-- GAPPED/ERRORED
collocation_pick       A: 'She ___ a photo of us at the beach.'  <-- GAPPED/ERRORED
word_bank_order        A: 'I went to the shops'
l1_to_l2_production    A: 'I went to the shop yesterday'
dictation              A: 'I forgot my keys and had to wait outside'
listening_gap          A: "She doesn't like coffee these days"
speak_repeat           A: "I'll call you back in a minute"
speak_answer           A: 'What did you do last weekend?'
match_pairs            (not judged — sentence_of returns "")

10 judged, 4 of them gapped or errored, 6 already prose.
```

Every `unnatural` verdict is a defective judged string. Every clean-prose string
passed. The fifth rejection, `listening_gap`, passed naturalness and failed at
the **probe** — a different gate, filed as **#121**.

**There is no threshold**, so the fix everyone reaches for first does not exist:
the verdict is a raw boolean and a missing row fails *open*.

### What is still unknown, and it is one question

**Does the judge accept the same sentence with the gap closed?** That is the
counterfactual, it is not derivable from code, and it is **arm B**. Until it is
run the finding is *cause identified*, not *cause proven* — **#115 is updated and
deliberately not closed.**

### Run W5b — on the Mac. It does not touch production.

This opens no database connection, writes nothing, and never contacts the shared
host. It needs only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the repo-root `.env`. **No backup, no
migration, no restart, no deploy.**

**1. Dry run. Sends nothing.**

```
python -m core.items.judge_observe
```

*Evidence:* the model name, the naturalness prompt in full, and both arms for
every fixture. Ends `Nothing was sent and nothing was written.` The four

### Deploy, then check — in this order

Nothing below has been run. Every step is the human's; Claude Code has no SSH
access to this host and is not to be given any. The host is shared with
`fonderis-worker`: no broad upgrades, no reboot, no Caddy rewrite.

1. **Backup.** `bash scripts/backup.sh` → a new dated dump and its R2 key.
2. **Pull** to the W6 commit; `git log --oneline -1`.
3. **`pip install -e packages/core`** → `Successfully installed core-…`.
4. **`pytest -q`** → no fewer than 1275 passing, zero failing. Record the total.
5. **`cd apps/web && pnpm install && pnpm test`** → the Vitest pass count, with

   trap #67 was opened for.**

    takes only `migrate` and `status`, and `.env` must not be sourced (#98). Run

    fixtures — including an `l1_to_l2_production` whose canonical is trusted, not
    verified (#102).

### W6's human checks — what each catches that no test can

1. **All eleven opened on a real phone, answered, feedback read.** Catches a
   projection that is complete and practically unanswerable — a word bank that
   does not fit the width, a `match_pairs` with no visible way to pair, an
   `error_spot` whose tiles wrap mid-sentence. No test can look at a layout and
   say a person could not do this.
   **What this check will NOT show:** no fixture carries an `explanation` and
   none declares an `error_type`, so the panel renders **the cue and the
   canonical answer for every item**. The record must say *the fallback* was
   verified, never *the panel* was (#103, #104).
2. **A typed answer with wrong capitalisation and a trailing full stop, on the
   phone's own keyboard with autocorrect live.** Catches the one thing Vitest
   cannot — jsdom has no autocorrect. `autoCorrect="off"` is a *request* to iOS
   Safari, and whether it is honoured for a given input is an empirical question
   about a real device. **This is the only place the autocorrect question can be
   settled.**
3. **One-handed tap reachability, and no layout shift when the keyboard opens.**
   Catches a submit button under the thumb-shadow or below the keyboard, and the
   iOS focus-zoom that a computed-style assertion approximates but cannot
   reproduce.
4. **The wrong-answer path read for guilt copy, by a person, in the app.**
   Catches what the regex cannot — tone. "That's not it" passes every banned
   pattern and still reads as a rebuke. A scan finds only words someone already
   thought to ban.
5. **`dictation` and `listening_gap` played with the phone on silent, and on
   mobile data.** Catches an audio element that plays in desktop Chrome and is
   blocked by iOS autoplay policy or the hardware mute switch, and a synthesis
   latency that is fine on wifi and not on 4G.
6. **The accept-rate table read as a number.** Catches nothing — that is the
   point. It is the first real datum for W10, and it licenses **no claim about
   the gate's rate**: eleven items, one sample each, of a stochastic system.
7. **The purge confirmed** (step 13). Catches the failure that would otherwise
   surface at W10 as a learner being taught from a test fixture.
